findings.title: All 14 success criteria mapped to tasks with correct test-with sequencing
findings.description: Every success criterion from the slice design traces to at least one task: SC1→1.1, SC2→1.2, SC3/4→1.3, SC5→1.4 (round-trip test), SC6→2.1/2.3, SC7/8→2.2/2.3, SC9→2.2/2.3, SC10→3.2/3.4 (mock test), SC11→3.4 (integration tests), SC12→4.1/4.2, SC13→3.5/5.1, SC14→5.2. Implementation tasks are immediately followed by their test tasks in each section, and commit markers sit after tested points (Sections 1, 2, 3, 4) — not after every task and not only at the end. Sequencing respects dependencies: config enum/field before enforcement module, enforcement module before simulation wiring, wiring before config defaults, defaults before final verification.

findings.title: Task granularity and proportionality fit a 2/5 effort slice
findings.description: The task file covers 6 source files and 3 test files across 5 sections. Task 2.3 is the largest (many parametrized cases) but each case maps directly to SC6–9 edge conditions explicitly named in the slice (half-open wrap, multi-width overshoot, idempotent reflect). Task 3.4 is dense but covers SC10–11 which demand both mock-verified OPEN-skipping and 50+ tick integration assertions. No task is so large it should be split, and no task is so granular it should be merged. No scope creep: the non-string validation in Task 1.3 traces to the slice's "If present, must be a string" requirement, and the idempotent-velocity reflect test traces to the slice's deliberate `abs`/`-abs` design note.

findings.title: No load test required — no restated NFR in the slice
findings.description: The slice discusses "zero overhead" for the OPEN path as a design goal rather than a formal non-functional requirement, and there is no performance NFR restated in the success criteria. No load test task in `tests/load/` is needed for this slice.
